l0_override.reason: The course scores the skill set with its own criteria A1-A8, which replace the generic D1-D8.

criteria.name: Structure
criteria.pass_when: Each skill is one kebab-case folder with a SKILL.md file of exactly that name
criteria.details:
Pass when ALL skills satisfy:
- Folder name: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only (regex ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$), at most 64 characters
- Exactly 1 file named exactly "SKILL.md" at the root of the skill folder
Fail when: the folder name has uppercase letters, spaces, "_" or Vietnamese diacritics; the file is named skill.md, SKILL.MD or SKILL.md.txt; SKILL.md sits in a subfolder

criteria.name: Frontmatter
criteria.pass_when: Has name and description; name matches the folder name
criteria.details:
Pass when:
- SKILL.md starts with "---" on line 1, has a closing "---", and the YAML parses without error
- Has "name", IDENTICAL to the folder name (case-sensitive)
- Has a non-empty "description" of at most 1024 characters, containing no < or > characters
Fail when: the frontmatter or its closing "---" is missing; name is "Test Case Generation" but the folder is "test-case-generation"; the frontmatter is not on line 1
Note: extra keys (license, metadata, ...) do not make it fail

criteria.name: Description
criteria.pass_when: States clearly when to use the skill ("Use when...")
criteria.details:
Pass when:
- Has a trigger clause: "Use when..." / "Use this skill when..."
- Names the concrete ACTIVITY + INPUT (e.g. "reviewing a user story before designing test cases")
- Read on its own, the description does not overlap with another skill in the course
Fail when: it only says what the skill is ("This skill generates test cases"); the trigger clause is too generic ("Use when testing"); the trigger condition is only written in the SKILL.md body
Recommended (no deduction): also state the output (e.g. "exports as Excel")

criteria.name: Process
criteria.details:
Pass when:
- SKILL.md has a heading Process / Workflow / Steps
- Steps are numbered continuously from 1, with no skipped or repeated numbers, and at least 3 steps
- Each step starts with an action verb (Extract, Identify, Export, ...)
Fail when: written as a paragraph or as unnumbered "-" bullets; numbers skipped or repeated (1,2,4); the process only lives in a references file
Note: sub-steps (2a, 2b, bullets nested inside one step) are accepted

criteria.name: File-opening instructions
criteria.pass_when: Every file in references/ and assets/ exists and says which step opens it
criteria.na_when: N/A when: the skill has neither references/ nor assets/
criteria.details:
Pass when:
- Every file in references/ and assets/ is mentioned in SKILL.md by relative path (e.g. references/tc-writing-rules.md)
- Every path mentioned in SKILL.md exists (correct spelling, correct case)
- Each file states which step opens it ("Step N"), or is mentioned inside the content of step N; that step number must exist in the Process
Fail when: an "orphan" file is never mentioned; a link is broken; only a generic "see references folder" is given; files are listed without saying which step
N/A when: the skill has neither references/ nor assets/

criteria.name: Files in the right place
criteria.pass_when: references/ holds rules/checklists; templates live in assets/
criteria.details:
Pass when:
- Skill folder root: only SKILL.md (LICENSE allowed)
- references/: documents for Claude to READ (rules, checklists, guides, formats), .md/.txt
- assets/: files to USE/COPY into the output (.xlsx/.docx templates, images)
- scripts/: runnable code (.py/.sh)
- No stray folders (docs/, templates/, ...), no lock files such as ~$*.xlsx, no output files already filled with data
Fail when: an Excel template sits in references/ or at the root; a checklist .md sits in assets/; a .py file sits in references/
Note: sample code written INSIDE a references .md file is still accepted

criteria.name: No domain knowledge
criteria.pass_when: No AUT name, URL, test account or project business rule in the skill
criteria.details:
Scan scope: SKILL.md, references/, scripts/ AND the content inside assets/ (cells, hidden sheets, dropdowns of the template)
Fail when any of these appear:
- A real AUT / product / customer name
- A URL, domain, IP, or environment name (staging, UAT server, ...)
- A test account, password, token or API key
- A project business rule written as a rule (e.g. "a cart holds at most 20 items")
- A fixed project list: modules, screens, known issues, ticket IDs
Allowed: general QA principles; the team's generic template format; illustrative examples marked "e.g."; placeholders such as <AUT name>
Test: "If I used this skill on a different project, would this sentence still be true?" If not, it fails

criteria.name: No overlap
criteria.pass_when: No two skills have descriptions covering the same scope (N/A when there is only 1 skill)
criteria.na_when: N/A when: there is only 1 skill
criteria.details:
N/A when: there is only 1 skill
How to check: compare the descriptions pair by pair; for each skill write one typical request and see whether it also matches the other skill's description
A pair passes when:
- The ACTIVITY or the INPUT differs; or
- If the input is the same, the description states a boundary (e.g. "before designing test cases", "from the output of ...", "Do NOT use for ...")
Fail when: two descriptions are near-paraphrases of each other; one description swallows the other ("Use for any QA task")

criteria.name: Clarification questions
criteria.pass_when: An output exists, and the chat evidence shows the skill produced it
criteria.details:
Pass when BOTH hold:
1. Output exists: the Markdown analysis in the chat has a "Clarification questions" section split into 2 groups, "Must ask" and "Nice to confirm", each with at least 1 question (a group with no question must say "None" with a reason)
2. Evidence the skill produced it: the transcript shows the test-requirements-analysis skill being invoked (skill name in a tool call, or Claude reading that skill's SKILL.md), and the questions appear in Claude's answer RIGHT AFTER that invocation, in the same chat
Fail when: only a screenshot or text file of the questions is submitted, with no transcript; the questions were typed into the chat by the trainee; the questions are not split into Must ask / Nice to confirm; the transcript is cut and the skill-invocation part is missing

criteria.name: TR list
criteria.pass_when: A TR file exists, and the evidence shows the skill produced it
criteria.details:
Pass when ALL 3 hold:
1. An .xlsx file exists with a sheet "Test Requirement" and the columns: AC ID | Acceptance Criteria | TR ID | Test Requirements | Notes, with at least 1 data row
2. The transcript shows the test-requirements-analysis skill being invoked, and the same chat contains the Python code that creates the file (file name in the code = submitted file name)
3. The file was created by copying the template from assets/ (keeping the title "Requirements Traceability Matrix", styles and column widths), not rebuilt from scratch
Fail when: no transcript; the submitted file name does not match the file created in the chat; columns are missing or the sheet name is wrong; the file was made by hand by the trainee
Note: hand edits after the skill created the file are allowed (graded under critical thinking), but the structure must be kept and the trainee must record what they changed

criteria.name: TC list
criteria.pass_when: A TC file exists, and the evidence shows the skill produced it
criteria.details:
Pass when ALL 4 hold:
1. An .xlsx file exists with a sheet "TC List" and the columns: TR ID | TC ID | TC Summary | Pre-Condition | Steps | Expected Result | Notes, with at least 1 data row
2. The transcript shows the test-case-generation skill being invoked, and the same chat contains the Python code that creates the file (file name in the code = submitted file name)
3. The file was created by copying the template from assets/ (keeping the title "Test Case List", styles and column widths)
4. The workflow chains: every TR ID value in the TC file exists in the TR file submitted for B2 (proving the TC file was generated from the TR file, not run independently)
Fail when: no transcript; file name mismatch; columns missing or wrong sheet name; a TR ID in the TC file is not in the TR file
Note: hand edits after the skill created the file are allowed if the structure is kept and the trainee records what they changed

criteria.name: Bug report
criteria.pass_when: A bug report exists, and the evidence shows the skill produced it
criteria.details:
Pass when ALL 3 hold:
1. The chat has a Markdown analysis with all 5 sections: Evidence Reviewed | Error Patterns & Root Cause Hypotheses | Facts vs. Assumptions vs. Hypotheses | Impact, Severity & Priority Assessment | Missing Information & Recommended Next Investigation
2. An .xlsx file exists with a sheet "Bug List" and all 14 columns: ID | Summary | Description | Pre-Condition | Steps to Reproduce | Screenshot | Build found | Reproducibility | Severity | Frequency | Priority | Keyword | Status | Note, with at least 1 bug, and the dropdowns kept from the template
3. The transcript shows the defect-analysis-reporting skill being invoked, with the original evidence (screenshot/log) uploaded, and the same chat contains the Python code that creates the file (file name matches)
Fail when: one of the 2 outputs (Markdown or Excel) is missing; a section is missing; no transcript; the file was not created from the template; the original evidence in the chat differs from the evidence the trainee submitted

criteria.name: Clarification questions
criteria.pass_when: Identifies the ambiguous points in the answer key; splits "Must ask" and "Nice to confirm"
criteria.details:
Compare against: the list of ambiguous points in the answer key
Matching rule: a question matches if it asks about exactly that ambiguous point, wording need not match; a question that combines several points counts for each point
Pass when ALL hold:
- At least 70% of all ambiguous points are found
- Every Mandatory ambiguous point the trainee found sits in "Must ask", not in "Nice to confirm"
- Both groups "Must ask" and "Nice to confirm" are present
Fail when: a Mandatory ambiguous point is missed; a Mandatory ambiguous point is placed in "Nice to confirm"; a question is generic and names no ambiguous point ("Is there anything else required?")
Note: a sensible question that is not in the answer key is not penalised; record it so the answer key can be updated

criteria.name: TR list
criteria.pass_when: Every ambiguous point or edge case in the answer key has a TR row; each TR traces to an AC or N/A
criteria.details:
Compare against: the ACs in the user story + the ambiguous points in the answer key
Pass when ALL hold:
- Every AC in the user story has at least 1 TR row
- At least 70% of all ambiguous points have a matching TR row
- 100% of TR rows have a correct AC ID (that AC really exists in the user story) or say "N/A"; N/A rows must have Notes naming the origin (Edge case / Risk / Assumption / Missing info)
Fail when: an AC has no TR; a Mandatory ambiguous point has no TR; a TR cites an AC ID that does not exist; an edge case is attached to an unrelated AC instead of being marked N/A

criteria.name: TC coverage
criteria.pass_when: Every TR has at least 1 TC; edge cases have their own TC
criteria.details:
Compare against: the trainee's own TR file + the edge cases in the answer key
Pass when ALL hold:
- Every TR ID in the TR file appears at least once in the TR ID column of the TC file (check each ID)
- Every TR row whose Notes say "Edge case" has at least 1 dedicated TC, i.e. a TC Summary aimed at exactly that edge case, not merged into a happy-path TC
- Every Mandatory edge case in the answer key has at least 1 TC testing it
Fail when: a TR has no TC; an edge case is only mentioned inside another TC; a TR is marked BLOCKED with no accompanying TC and no stated reason
Note: a TR marked BLOCKED may have a TC carrying a BLOCKED flag, which still counts as covered

criteria.name: TC quality
criteria.pass_when: Expected Result is specific, never "works correctly"
criteria.details:
Compare against: the whole Expected Result column (if more than 50 TCs: check all edge-case TCs plus a random 20 of the rest)
An Expected Result is specific when it states at least 1 observable thing: message content, displayed value, screen navigated to, field/button state, data saved or not saved
Phrases forbidden when standing alone: "works correctly/properly/as expected", "displayed correctly", "no error", "success", "OK"
Pass when: 0 Expected Results violate this, and Steps contain concrete test data (not a generic "enter valid data")
Fail when: at least 1 Expected Result violates this. Record the TC ID with a quote, one error per violating Expected Result

criteria.name: Bug finding
criteria.pass_when: Finds at least N bugs from the answer key's bug list
criteria.details:
Compare against: the planted bug list in the answer key (BUG-xx), each with a severity label
Matching rule: a trainee bug matches a BUG-xx if it has the right location and the right symptom; several reports of the same cause count once
N = 60% of all BUG-xx rounded up (baseline.thresholds.bug_found_pct), e.g. 5 bugs gives N = 3
Pass when ALL hold:
- At least N matching bugs found
- 100% of the Critical/Major bugs found
Fail when: fewer than N matching bugs, or a Critical/Major bug is missed
Note: a bug outside the answer key that the grader confirms is real is recorded but does not count toward N; a bug that cannot be reproduced or is correct behaviour per the spec is recorded in grading_notes as a false positive

criteria.name: Bug report
criteria.pass_when: Each bug has steps, expected/observed, severity and priority with reasons; no invented environment information
criteria.details:
Compare against: every bug in the Bug List file + the exam document (the list of environment information the exam provides)
Pass when EACH bug satisfies:
- Steps to Reproduce: numbered, start from a clear initial state, someone else can follow them
- Has both an Expected Result and an Observed Result, and the two differ
- Severity and Priority come from the dropdown values, each with its own reason (in Note or in the Markdown "Impact, Severity & Priority")
- Build found / browser / OS: filled in only if the exam provides it; if not, left empty with "not provided" in Note
Fail when: a bug lacks steps / expected / observed; Severity or Priority has no reason; environment information that is not in the exam is filled in (invented)
Severity deviating by more than 1 level from the answer key is NOT an error here: it is an advisory flag (C6-severity) that a human decides

advisory.text: A bug's severity deviates by more than 1 level from the answer key's severity (per baseline.severity_scale)
advisory.note: The agent only records the flag with the bug ID, the trainee's severity and the key's severity. A human decides pass/fail; until then it costs no points and the report is provisional.

criteria.name: No fabrication
criteria.pass_when: No rule is presented as a requirement when the user story does not state it
criteria.details:
Compare against: the verbatim user story / ACs of the exam + the Notes of TR/TC
How to check: list every concrete rule appearing in the TR, Expected Results and Steps (limits, lengths, formats, error message content, permissions, processing order), then look for each one in the user story
Pass when: every rule NOT in the user story is marked "Assumption —" or "BLOCKED —", or is put into a clarification question
Fail when: at least 1 rule that is not in the user story is written as a confirmed requirement
Failing example: the user story says nothing about password length, but a TC states Expected "Shows error 'Password must be 8-20 characters'" with no Assumption flag
